Something historic happened at Flushing Meadows on Sunday — and it hasn't happened in three decades.

Ben Shelton. Frances Tiafoe. Alex Michelsen. Three American men are in the US Open quarterfinals, giving the United States its deepest men's run at a major since 1995. Five Americans were in the round of 16 this year — the most since that same era.

Shelton was dominant. He took out Stefanos Tsitsipas 6-2, 6-3, 6-4 in an hour and a half — next up, he faces defending champion Carlos Alcaraz. Tiafoe overcame former US Open champion Daniil Medvedev in a tough three-setter, saving two tiebreaks along the way. And 20-year-old Alex Michelsen — the tournament's surprise quarterfinalist — kept rolling past Tomas Etcheverry.

The last American man to win a Grand Slam was Andy Roddick right here at the US Open in 2003. Could this be the year that drought ends?

Tiafoe and Michelsen face each other in an all-American QF — so at minimum, one American reaches the semifinal. Then there's Shelton, who has the power to take down Alcaraz. 🎾🇺🇸

What a moment for U.S. tennis. Are you watching?

The women's quarterfinals are set — and they don't get much better than this.

Aryna Sabalenka, the two-time defending US Open champion, is on course for a historic three-peat. She won her fourth-round match over Taylor Townsend convincingly, and her next opponent is Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova. No woman has won three consecutive US Open titles since Serena Williams did it from 2012 to 2014.

Meanwhile, Jessica Pegula and Emma Navarro — both Americans — will face each other in the quarterfinals, guaranteeing at least one U.S. woman in the semifinals. Pegula has been one of the most consistent players in the draw; Navarro has had a stunning run.

Could the US Open end with American men AND women in the semis? 🎾

Monday at the US Open is going to be must-watch tennis.

The final fourth-round matches complete the quarterfinal draw today, and the schedule is loaded. Here's what to watch:

🎾 Iga Swiatek vs. Zheng Qinwen (Arthur Ashe Stadium, 11:30 AM ET) — A rematch of the Paris Olympics semifinal, where Zheng upset Swiatek on the way to gold. Swiatek wants revenge; Zheng wants to prove it wasn't a fluke.

🎾 Elena Rybakina vs. Naomi Osaka (Louis Armstrong, not before 2:30 PM ET) — Rybakina came into this US Open fighting an ankle injury and has survived every round so far. Now she faces Osaka, who has had a remarkable comeback season.

🎾 Coco Gauff vs. Iva Jovic (Arthur Ashe Stadium night session, not before 7 PM ET) — An all-American showdown. Jovic just beat Alexandra Eala in a three-set thriller last night. Gauff is the fan favorite, but Jovic is rolling.

On the men's side: No. 1 seed Alexander Zverev faces Luciano Darderi in the evening session on Ashe, and 20-year-old Learner Tien — the youngest American man in the US Open R4 since Roddick in 2002 — takes on Karen Khachanov.

By tonight, all eight women's quarterfinalists and all eight men's quarterfinalists will be set. 🎾

Alex Eala's historic US Open run came to an end Saturday night at Arthur Ashe Stadium — but what a run it was.

Iva Jovic defeated Eala 7-5, 3-6, 7-5 in three hours and three minutes in one of the most intense matches of the tournament. Jovic won five of the last six games to close it out and extended her head-to-head advantage over Eala to 3-0.

Eala entered this tournament as the No. 17 seed — the highest Grand Slam seeding in Philippine tennis history. She reached the third round at Flushing Meadows, further than any Filipino woman has ever gone at a Grand Slam. She played at Arthur Ashe Stadium in primetime. She gave Jovic everything she had for three hours.

That's not a loss to hang your head about. That's the start of something. 🎾🇵🇭

What a statement from Eala at this US Open.

🎾 Aryna Sabalenka vs. Linda Noskova — Three-peat bid vs. Wimbledon champion. History on the line.
🎾 Jessica Pegula vs. Emma Navarro — Another all-American QF. One of them is going to the semis.
